prereg_e_calibration.calibrate_unit chooses its logic by the unit NAME. Called with unit = corpus name, it skips N1, N5 and F3 and has no error definition (error_classes returns 'no_definition'), so it cannot produce the N1 bounds or N5 truncation constants that splits.new_corpora requires. The primary calibration therefore uses calibrate_unit(corpus, 'cc_local', u). cc_local is the same Claude Code generation: hooks are hook_* attachments with toolUseID, and these corpora have 0 progress entries. The literal-unit result is stored beside it as a reference. Side effect of the proxy: private_key masking of non-public tool names (labels only).

splits.new_corpora.calibration lists Probe 1 floors/G90, Probe 3 L75 and Probe 2 D_unit, but calibrate_unit computes none of them. I also called prereg_calibration.probe1_unit, probe2_unit and probe3_unit with the proxy and stored their raw outputs (phase_b_unit_functions). The D_unit resolution rule was not applied. L75 is 111 for pub_cc_hf and 251 for pub_trace_commons.

problems: BLINDNESS DISCLOSURE: before the split existed, while designing the loader, I ran exploratory scratch scans over ALL raw files of both corpora. These were a structural survey, credential-pattern counts with variable names, value lengths and character shapes, a character-level diff-shape comparison of the armand0e and cfahlgren1 copies, and JSON secret-field counts. No timing, latency, request-id bracket, error or mechanism quantity was computed, but B/E/H content was opened. The committed loader's population pass also reads every file's structure by design (ids, types, timestamps, tool ids, model strings, fingerprints; no content kept). Separately, Track B (B5e) already computed request-id decode deltas and call-to-result gap quantiles over these full corpora (CORPUS_INVENTORY 2.5), so R1, latency and N3 results on E for these corpora are not fully blind with respect to B5e.

An earlier run of my loader wrote a different B/E/H draw (largest feasible floor). I replaced it with the shared min(5, n//cells) rule before any B/E/H session was parsed. A was identical under both rules, and the A caches are byte-identical. The orchestrator should log the floor deviation once for all new corpora.

Decisions only the orchestrator can make before any B/E read: (1) accept or override the 'cc_local' format-proxy unit for these corpora; the measurement scripts must pass the same proxy to the prereg functions. (2) Add a session_cluster_map branch for new corpora (cluster = stratum) if repo dominance and confinement should be testable. (3) Append both prereg_e_extensions records to the change_log; I did not edit prereg_e.json, HELDOUT_MANIFEST.json or any lib/ file.

surprises: Deep-Agents__GPT-5.2-Codex ATIF timestamps are not event times. In all 7 A sessions every step stamp falls within 0.2-1.3 ms of the others, 17,999.99 s (5 h) after result.json agent_execution.finished_at. They look like local time written as UTC at conversion. The loader applies a generic rule: an ATIF file with >=3 stamped steps spanning under 1 s gets ts None and ts_kind 'none', and the raw stamp goes to extra.atif_write_stamp. surprises: Split rule vs lib/sample floor: lib/sample._alloc applies a floor of min(5, cell size) per cell even when the floors add up to more than the split total. calibrate_unit() keys its format rules on the unit name. So the new corpora are calibrated under their pre-registered analogue: pub_codex as 'swechat/codex', agentcap OpenCode sessions as 'swechat/opencode'. A side effect: field_gate() then reports external_commit_table=True and external_usage_tally=True, inherited from swechat. These are corrected to False in resolved.n6_field_gate_A (listed in n6_field_gate_corrections); the raw unit_result keeps calibrate_unit's own output.

Pi has no pre-registered analogue. It is calibrated as 'agentcap/pi', which means no N1 bounds and no N5 items (it is not in LAT_UNITS or N5_UNITS), and error_classes returns no_definition even though Pi records a native isError on 1,522 of 1,522 A results.

AC4 dominance is degenerate for any new corpus: session_cluster_map falls back to a single cluster, so dominated_at_A is always True. Uploader/run dominance is computed separately in the build reports. pub_codex is dominated by one uploader (kingkw1: 49% of A calls; one session alone holds 36%). agentcap is not dominated by run (top run 15%), but by suite it is: transformers-coding holds 62% of A calls.

agentcap clocks (descriptive, A only): captured_at falls before the trace's response-end stamp (median -4.19 s, q0.01 -69.3 s), so it is not a capture-at-response time. The calls are lib/sample._alloc with floor min(5, n // cells) and default_rng(20261006). The result equals the saved A/B/E/H for every corpus, and every size equals the pre-registered formula. Every calibration sha256 matches its extension record. ir.validate passes on all 6 A caches. Each A cache's session set equals its A ids. No <corpus>_{B,E,H} cache or newcorp_build_<corpus>_{B,E}.json exists anywhere under C:\Swarms (data/ excluded) or in TEMP.
